<reason>PRO kept the written comparison live: markets ration repair and skip unsellable rupture records, while governments already hold much of the paper and can fund access with community rules. CON’s consent/capture critique was sharp and rhetorically stronger, but it leaned on a monopoly-unredacted-commons reading PRO disclaimed, its opening was clipped, and grants/licenses never fully answered who produces a usable copy of the ledger that does not sell.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO’s structural turn that CON only wins by collapsing “digitize and publicly fund access” into one ministry posting sealed files, plus the live weighing that an allotment roll that never becomes a product has no second key.</best_rebuttal>
